title: P1 - Updates (Post ES26)

content.text: Pillar-1 updates from Budget-2026 & Economic Survey 2026 (ES26), on top of the P1A1-P1D3 notes.
market crossed $300 billion (2025); prices linked to real/financial assets -> risk of negative spillover to the economy.
CRR cuts + OMO gave banks more liquidity, so they borrow less via MSF and park more in SDF.
Net Bank Credit to Govt + Bank Credit to Commercial Sector + Net Forex Assets of banking sector + Govt currency liabilities - Net Non-Monetary Liabilities (remember NCERT version for prelims).

new 'Banking Reforms for Viksit Bharat' committee; merger of Power Ministry NBFCs PFC + REC (like Dena/Vijaya into BoB).

MFIs (loan up to Rs.1.25 lakh rural / Rs.2 lakh urban) push loans to hit targets while claiming women-empowerment impact.
an NBFC need NOT register with RBI if asset size <= Rs.1,000 cr AND it takes no public funds AND has no customer interface.
S&P upgraded India's insolvency regime from Group C to Group B (2025); better borrower behaviour; IBC Amendment Bill 2025 (cross-border insolvency).
cases take 713-853 days (target 330); NCLT flooded with 30,000+ cases; under half of 4,500+ Insolvency Professionals are active.

contentText: What this is:  Pillar-1 updates from Budget-2026 & Economic Survey 2026 (ES26), on top of the P1A1-P1D3 notes. 1. Money, Money Supply & Monetary Policy Stablecoins (ES26):  market crossed $300 billion (2025); prices linked to real/financial assets -> risk of negative spillover to the economy. MSF down, SDF up (ES26):  CRR cuts + OMO gave banks more liquidity, so they borrow less via MSF and park more in SDF. M3 formula (ES):  Net Bank Credit to Govt + Bank Credit to Commercial Sector + Net Forex Assets of banking sector + Govt currency liabilities - Net Non-Monetary Liabilities (remember NCERT version for prelims). Q - RBI MPC (Feb-2026) key decisions? Matter Reform E-banking fraud Up to Rs.25,000 compensation to the customer Repo rate Unchanged at 5.25% (stance Neutral) Urban Cooperative Banks Mission SAKSHAM (Sahakari Bank Kshamta Nirman) - staff skilling Kisan Credit Card loan tenure 5 -> 6 years Collateral-free loan to Micro & Small Enterprises Rs.10 lakh -> Rs.20 lakh Bank lending to REITs Now allowed (earlier only InvITs) Financial Literacy Week 2026 theme 'KYC - Your First Step to Safe Banking' 2. Banks & NBFCs Budget-2026:  new 'Banking Reforms for Viksit Bharat' committee; merger of Power Ministry NBFCs PFC + REC (like Dena/Vijaya into BoB). RRB merger (ES26):  196 -> 28 Regional Rural Banks ('One-State-One-RRB'); common logo; higher profitability, lower NPA. Micro-finance 'impact-washing' (ES26):  MFIs (loan up to Rs.1.25 lakh rural / Rs.2 lakh urban) push loans to hit targets while claiming women-empowerment impact. NBFC registration exemption (2026):  an NBFC need NOT register with RBI if asset size <= Rs.1,000 cr AND it takes no public funds AND has no customer interface. 3. NPA, IBC & AI IBC (ES26) - positives:  S&P upgraded India's insolvency regime from Group C to Group B (2025); better borrower behaviour; IBC Amendment Bill 2025 (cross-border insolvency). IBC (ES26) - negatives:  cases take 713-853 days (target 330); NCLT flooded with 30,000+ cases; under half of 4,500+ Insolvency Professionals are active. FREE-AI:  RBI's Pushpak Bhattacharyya Committee - 'Framework for Responsible & Ethical Enablement of AI'; 7 Sutras (Trust; People First; Innovation over restraint; Fairness; Accountability; Understandable by design; Safety/resilience). 4. Bonds, TReDS & Share Market TReDS (Budget-2026):  CPSE purchases from MSMEs routed via TReDS; CGTMSE credit guarantee; GeM linked to TReDS; a secondary market for TReDS receipts. Budget-2026:  Rs.100-200 cr bonus to ULBs issuing municipal bonds; CPSE real-estate monetized via REITs; higher tax on F&O derivatives. Share market (ES26):  21.6 cr DEMAT accounts (1/4 women); household savings in shares/MFs rose 2% (2012) -> 15% (2025). FSAP (IMF+World Bank, 2025):  Indian capital-market size 144% (2017) -> 175% of GDP (2024); banks/NBFCs have adequate capital buffers. Corporate bond market (ES26):  still shallow (~16-17% of GDP vs China 36%, US 40%, Korea 79%) -> high bank dependence = systemic risk. FII vs DII (ES26):  FIIs were net SELLERS (sold ~Rs.16.5 lakh cr, 2025); DIIs were net BUYERS (own 18.3% of Indian shares). IPOs as 'exit vehicles' (ES26):  of Rs.1.60 lakh cr raised via IPOs (2025), 58% was Offer-for-Sale (founders exiting, not fresh capital). CEA: reducing the cost of capital needs a manufacturing push, not just deepening the capital market. 5. Insurance, Pension & Gig Workers Insurance (ES26):  'low-penetration, high-cost' - density $97/person (rising), penetration 3.7% of GDP (stagnant/falling); high customer-acquisition cost (offline agents) and poor renewals; needs digital distribution. Pension (ES26):  60+ population 10.1% (2021) -> 14.9% (2036); India's pension assets ~17% of GDP vs ~80% in advanced economies. NPS e-Shramik model (PFRDA, 2025):  to enrol gig/platform workers into NPS. Key Facts (Quick Revision) Fact Detail RRB merger 196 -> 28 (One-State-One-RRB). MSE collateral-free loan Raised to Rs.20 lakh (Feb-2026). KCC loan tenure 6 years (from 5). Bank lending to REITs Now allowed. FREE-AI RBI Pushpak Bhattacharyya Committee; 7 Sutras. IPOs 2025 58% of IPO value was Offer-for-Sale (exits). Insurance Density $97; penetration 3.7% of GDP. Pension assets India ~17% of GDP vs advanced ~80%.
